items.title: John Casimir Interview, 1959-01-17
items.q: Getting old now. Kid Punch. He's somewhere in the out of town.

ctx.x: But Eddie, what the dialer player out there in Baton Rouge was a took jaw from him. Eddie Marsh played around him with Kid Punch in there. He's a good company man. Getting old now. Kid Punch. He's somewhere in the out of town.
Oh yeah, I got his address if you have a loan.

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1957-multiple
items.q: John Casimir has been marching for them every column.

ctx.x: Lots of them. I had a club called The Buzzards. Yeah. I played for them every column. Every column. When I finished this column, you make a contract for the next column. That's true. And one thing I must say, I left kind of on a sudden there, see, and I had to contract for them and I could never come back. But I don't see none of them. That Gundolfa fella, I'll tell you about that, he was the head of that. Well that's still going.
John Casimir has been marching for them every column.

But I mean the fella I always played, I didn't find out that John, John, Gundolfa, anyway, Gundolfa. Joe Gundolfa, I asked you about it. They have different bands every Saturday night. Yeah, I should play out on the lake for them all, every Sunday, pretty much when you didn't have to play a parade or something, but down the street show. But see how it goes them days, if you signed a contract with a man there for advertising and another man wants you for a parade, why don't you just call up some of the other…
